comparisons.peer_topic: LIBOR Antitrust Litigation Status and Claims
comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup and Citibank are defendants in multi-district litigation alleging manipulation of USD LIBOR; while many actions were dismissed or settled, surviving plaintiffs assert Sherman Act and state law claims seeking compensatory damages.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C are defendants in multi-district litigation regarding U.S. Dollar LIBOR manipulation in the S.D.N.Y. Both cite antitrust claims (Sherman Act) as the surviving basis for litigation. However, BAC's disclosure focuses on pending motions for summary judgment for remaining individual and class claims, whereas C's disclosure highlights that many actions were previously dismissed or settled, with survivors asserting Sherman Act and state law claims.

sentences.text: Beginning in 2011, several individual and putative class actions were filed against the Corporation, BANA, and certain Merrill Lynch entities, as well as other banks on the U.S. Dollar LIBOR panel.

Defendants' motion for summary judgment is pending on all remaining claims, brought by individual plaintiffs and one class of plaintiffs who purchased over-the-counter instruments incorporating LIBOR.

Citigroup and Citibank, along with other U.S. Dollar (USD) LIBOR panel banks, are defendants in a multi-district litigation proceeding before the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York captioned IN RE LIBOR-BASED FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS ANTITRUST LITIGATION.
Plaintiffs with surviving claims against Citigroup and Citibank assert claims under the Sherman Act and state law based on allegations that defendants suppressed or otherwise manipulated USD LIBOR.

peer_results.rationale: Retrieved candidates (D509, D546) concern foreign exchange auctions and credit default swaps, which are distinct benchmarks and legal theories from the target's LIBOR manipulation topic.

comparisons.peer_summary: The monetary relief class action settled for ~$6.2 billion with $700 million returned to defendants; a separate injunctive class action saw preliminary approval denied in June 2024, while individual actions by opting merchants have mostly settled representing over 70% of sales volume. Ongoing matters include a Swiss EURIBOR investigation and a U.S. Court of Appeals affirmation of a dismissal in an antitrust lawsuit; the Firm has resolved all non-U.S. dollar LIBOR actions and obtained dismissals or moved for summary judgment in remaining U.S. dollar LIBOR cases.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose ongoing U.S. dollar LIBOR litigation in the S.D.N.Y. JPM reports more advanced resolution milestones, including a specific lawsuit dismissal affirmed on appeal in December 2024 and a $6.2 billion settlement of a separate interchange class action. In contrast, BAC's disclosure indicates that its motions for summary judgment on all remaining claims are still pending, suggesting its litigation exposure is at a different procedural stage than JPM's resolved or affirmed items.

sentences.text: All remaining cases are pending in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

Defendants' motion for summary judgment is pending on all remaining claims, brought by individual plaintiffs and one class of plaintiffs who purchased over-the-counter instruments incorporating LIBOR.
In addition, the Firm has been named as a defendant along with other banks in various individual and putative class actions related to benchmark rates, including U.S. dollar LIBOR.

In addition, a lawsuit filed by a group of individual plaintiffs asserting antitrust claims, alleging that the Firm and other defendants were engaged in an unlawful agreement to set U.S. dollar LIBOR and conspired to monopolize the market for LIBOR-based consumer loans and credit cards was dismissed in October 2023 and affirmed on appeal by the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit in December 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Interest Rate Swaps Antitrust Litigation Settlement
comparisons.peer_summary: In the In Re: Interest Rate Swaps Antitrust Litigation, the Firm reached an agreement in principle to settle class claims on February 28, 2024, following the court's denial of class certification on December 15, 2023. Preliminary approval of the settlement was granted by the court on July 11, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS disclose exposure to antitrust class actions in the S.D.N.Y. BAC's litigation is specific to LIBOR manipulation involving individual and class plaintiffs with pending summary judgment motions. MS's comparable disclosure (D322) relates to Interest Rate Swaps antitrust litigation, not LIBOR; however, the procedural posture is distinct as MS reached a settlement agreement in principle in February 2024 following denial of class certification, whereas BAC remains in the summary judgment phase for LIBOR.

sentences.text: Beginning in 2011, several individual and putative class actions were filed against the Corporation, BANA, and certain Merrill Lynch entities, as well as other banks on the U.S. Dollar LIBOR panel.

These actions alleged that defendants manipulated LIBOR during the financial crisis and asserted a variety of claims, including federal and state antitrust, Commodity Exchange Act, Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act, Securities Exchange Act of 1934, common law fraud, and breach of contract claims and sought compensatory, treble and punitive damages, and injunctive relief.

Beginning in February of 2016, the Firm was named as a defendant in multiple purported antitrust class actions now consolidated into a single proceeding in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York ("SDNY") styled In Re: Interest Rate Swaps Antitrust Litigation.
On December 29, 2023, the class plaintiffs petitioned the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit for leave to appeal that decision.
